== Biography ==

Dinah is Alice's beloved house cat, a quiet and gentle creature of the household. She is described as "a dear quiet thing," and she spends her days by the fire purring softly, licking her paws and washing her face.

Dinah is particularly skilled at catching mice—a talent Alice takes great pride in and is eager to demonstrate to others. At tea-time, she receives her saucer of milk as part of the household routine. Alice considers her "such a nice soft thing to nurse," suggesting that Dinah is an affectionate and pleasing companion.

Alice is deeply attached to Dinah, and when she finds herself in Wonderland, she feels the absence of her beloved pet keenly. She speaks eagerly of Dinah to the creatures she encounters, believing that anyone who saw her would come to appreciate cats. Alice even imagines, in her dreams during her fall through the rabbit-hole, questioning Dinah earnestly about whether she has ever eaten a bat.

In her predicament in Wonderland, Alice finds herself wishing that Dinah were present to help her, certain that her skilled companion could swiftly fetch the things she needs and that have gone astray.

== Narrative role ==

Dinah is [[Alice]]'s beloved pet cat, a dear and quiet creature who spends her days purring softly by the fire, licking her paws and washing her face. To hold her is a pleasure—she is such a nice soft thing to nurture—and she is uncommonly skilled at catching mice. While Alice ventures into Wonderland, Dinah remains at home, and Alice finds herself wishing her dear friend were there beside her in that strange land.

Though Dinah never travels to Wonderland herself, she becomes a figure of considerable power through the force of Alice's affection. When Alice speaks of her beloved cat to the animals she meets, including the Cheshire Cat, the mention of Dinah proves frightening enough to drive most of them away. Later, when Alice finds herself in confrontation with a crowd, she threatens to set Dinah upon them; the threat alone is sufficient to cause them to fall silent and abandon their efforts.

== Personality ==

Dinah embodies a quiet gentleness that defines her nature. Alice describes her as a "dear quiet thing," a creature inclined toward contentment and undemanding companionship. There is in Dinah a composed self-sufficiency, a fastidious attention to her person that speaks of a meditative, orderly temperament. She is, Alice insists, "such a nice soft thing to nurse"—an observation that speaks not only to her physical softness but to a suppleness of spirit, a willingness to offer comfort without complaint.

This serenity, however, conceals considerable capability. Dinah emerges as a skilled and focused hunter, earning Alice's repeated and emphatic praise as "such a capital one for catching mice." It is not casual prowess, but a competence born of attentiveness and precision. The same quiet creature who offers peaceful companionship possesses a sharp, efficient nature when called to act—a duality that marks her as both comfortable confidante and formidable presence.

Alice's faith in Dinah extends beyond mere hunting ability. She imagines Dinah possessed of such reliable capability that the cat would recover anything lost with swift certainty, suggesting a trust in both Dinah's competence and her dependability.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — beloved pet and cherished companion. Alice refers to Dinah as "our cat" and describes her with obvious warmth and devotion, valuing her gentle presence. Alice misses Dinah greatly while away and frequently recalls her fondly.

== Trivia ==

* Alice dreamed of Dinah whilst falling into Wonderland, asking her very earnestly whether she had ever eaten a bat.
* Dinah receives a saucer of milk at tea-time and sits purring by the fire, licking her paws and washing her face.
